title: State lives at a position in the tree

slides.say: You might think state lives inside your component. It actually lives inside React, tied to a position in the render tree.
Here one Counter tag is rendered at two positions. Each position gets its own state.

slides.text: Stop rendering a component and its state is destroyed. Render it again: it starts fresh.
slides.say: Stop rendering the second counter, and its state disappears completely. Render it again, and it starts from zero.

slides.text: React keeps state as long as the same component renders at the same position.
slides.say: Rule: React keeps state as long as the component is rendered at its position. Remove it, or render something else there, and the state is gone.
